title: Police cleared in man's death; SIU says Halton officers faced 'very real threat' but tried to subdue armed man before firing
article: Long-time friends of Steve Remian believe he committed"suicide by cop" when Halton officers shot him dead in an Oakville park last December.
Now, the province's Special Investigations Unit has cleared Halton Region police of wrongdoing in the death of Remian, who levelled a loaded rifle at them after a tense standoff in Wedgewood Park.
SIU Director James Cornish said the investigation showed officers acted when they were "faced with a very real threat of lethal force."

The news was cold comfort to acquaintances such as Ragna, a friend of Remian for 17 years. Like many of the friends he gathered as he wandered from job to job across western Canada, she said he was tormented by demons he couldn't overcome. "He had a lot of promise but he didn't have an easy life," said the 38-year-old Oakville woman, who asked that her last name not be published. "I don't believe he ever had any intention of pulling the trigger. I think he wanted the police to do it for him.

Remian, 38, was sobbing and had all his possessions in his battered, four-door Cadillac early on the morning of Dec. 1, 2007 when he brandished a rifle in front of people outside a Trafalgar Rd. coffee shop.

When he drove off, they called police, who tracked him to Wedgewood Park, next to the school he attended as a child. An officer shot out two tires of his car to prevent Remian from leaving the treed area.
After 15 minutes of trying to convince him to lay down his weapon - and after one officer used a Taser to try to subdue him - officers fired when Remian pointed the loaded .22-calibre rifle at them.
Police later found more than 400 rounds of ammunition in his car.
The SIU probes all incidents involving police and civilians that result in death or serious injury.

"These officers were dealing with a distraught, inconsolable and depressed man who that morning was preoccupied with self-destructive thoughts," Cornish said in a release issued yesterday. "The officers obviously had to isolate this man from other civilians given the fact that he was armed with a firearm. They could not simply retreat.
"That being said they did not rush the car," Cornish said. " Instead they chose what appears to have been their only reasonable option and that was to attempt to convince him to disarm and surrender.

"The officers carefully considered their use-of-force options and attempted to end this incident first by use of negotiation and tactical communication and then by less-lethal force through the Taser."
Friends said Remian had three children under 13 from whom he was estranged. He returned to Ontario just months before his death after losing a mining job in B.C.
Remian's name was raised last year at the B.C. murder trial of serial killer Willie Pickton after a suitcase and a hair of Remian's was found in a car on Pickton's pig farm.
Police determined the items were simply in the car of a friend that had been sold to Pickton for scrap.
